answer: Each epoch the network issues a fresh “comet” challenge: a cryptographic puzzle whose solution requires generating a unique proof‑of‑reasoning trace, recorded with a signed quill token and broadcast under a temporary lantern beacon. An agent must run its model on the challenge, submit the trace, and stake a deposit; only proofs that verify against the beacon are accepted as valid identities. An attacker therefore pays the full compute cost of solving the puzzle (≈ 10⁶ GPU‑seconds) plus the locked stake per fake, making each Sybil identity individually prohibitive.
